# HJsonViewer

> Bounded JSON inspection with expandable values and copyable JSON Pointer paths.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HJsonViewer` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-json-viewer>`.
- Constructor: `HearthJsonViewerElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Developer.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HJsonViewer.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Read-only inspection reuses HTreeView keyboard navigation. Select a node, then copy its value or RFC 6901 JSON Pointer path; root path is the empty string. Rendering is bounded by maxDepth=6 and maxEntries=300, reports cycles, and displays accessors without invoking them.
- Copy value uses normal JSON serialization; non-JSON/cyclic values report failure. Output over one million characters is rejected. The tree preview truncates long strings; copying uses the selected original value. The app owns editing and redaction.

## Public API

value: unknown · label, maxHeight: string · maxDepth, maxEntries: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    value: unknown;
    label?: string;
    maxDepth?: number;
    maxEntries?: number;
    maxHeight?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ label: "JSON data", maxDepth: 6, maxEntries: 300, maxHeight: "400px" }
```

### Events

select(string), copied(path | value), copy-error(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        path: string
    ];
    copied: [
        kind: "path" | "value"
    ];
    "copy-error": [
        message: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, viewport

Use `hearth-json-viewer::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HJsonViewer } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HJsonViewer label="Response payload" :value="{requestId:'req_42',status:'ok',metrics:{duration:42,cached:true},items:[1,2,3]}" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-json-viewer');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Response payload",
  "value": {
    "requestId": "req_42",
    "status": "ok",
    "metrics": {
      "duration": 42,
      "cached": true
    },
    "items": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ]
  }
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
